speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Progressive Wage Model (PWM)'s approach to wage increases is linked to an expectation of increased productivity from businesses, with the aim of reducing costs; and (b) what steps has the Ministry been taking to assist companies that have implemented the PWM and are facing difficulties in boosting productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: To do this, both workers and employers need to play their part, and they can tap on the range of resources and initiatives rolled out by the Government and tripartite partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Workers need to improve their skills so that they can be as efficient and as productive as they can be in their jobs, even as wage rises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Through upskilling, workers can also put themselves in a better position to take on larger and more complex job roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: And in particular, workers in PWM job roles are guided by the tripartite-endorsed PWM requirements on how best to upskill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: They are also supported by the Workfare Skills Support (WSS) Scheme, which provides training support to lower-wage workers, as well as the broader SkillsFuture movement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Beyond improving each worker's productivity directly through training, businesses must also take ownership in driving wider business transformations to improve productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Government recognises that the efforts to raise productivity take time and that, in the immediate term, businesses may face cost pressures arising from Progressive Wage moves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: As such, the Government has provided schemes to help businesses defray some of these costs in the transition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: As we expand PWM to uplift lower-wage workers, we will continue to support businesses to improve their productivity.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I wish to ask the Senior Minister of State, which PWM sectors have greatest potential for productivity increase and what is the Ministry doing to improve productivity for these sectors?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Thus far, all sectors with PWM have shown potential for improvements in productivity to achieve long-term sustainability, alongside uplifting wages for their lower-wage workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, each PWM sector has embarked on their respective transformation journeys and each one is backed by ITMs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Typically, when we look at even the recent ones like food service and retail, we have ITMs to back them up by the industry.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And these are also supported by Government and tripartite partners through various schemes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we want to make it a point that it is not just about the workers' productivity alone.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Because the workers can get skilled, trained and then, basically, they would be more productive, but they can only do so much if the business does not transform.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, you need the business to also move on the productivity drive because they can redesign jobs, they can put in place automation, sensors and so forth.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These are ways in which we can potentially improve the productivity levels.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But it is not just on the worker.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I would say that it is all three in tandem: the worker, the business, the industry.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: They would all have to transform at the same time and, therefore, you will see varying degrees of productivity improvements.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Hence, my point was, we do see good progress in terms of productivity.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Some of these take more time than others.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But there are certainly others that have greater potential.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And, therefore, this will enable service providers have greater flexibility to transform how they deliver services and bring in innovation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If you are just looking for the lowest cost at the maximum headcount, this is not going to help the industries either to transform.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That is why we were moving to outcomes based models.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This will help us also help the service providers improve business efficiency and productivity.
